decisions.reason: The rejection is correct: the cited result establishes uniqueness only for sequence limits, whereas the inverse A depends on a finite-subset net.  I repaired the load-bearing gap by proving net-limit uniqueness directly from the two tail conditions and the triangle inequality before defining A.

The rejection correctly identifies a false sentence, but the basis construction itself remains valid: if the kernel basis is empty no zero eigenvalue is needed.  I replaced the assertion by the conditional fact that each actual kernel-basis vector is nonzero and witnesses eigenvalue zero.

The rejection is correct under the supplied dimension interface: the finite-rank identity must name the common scalar field.  I changed the multiplicity to dim_F and also made explicit the compactness and nth-term facts used by the surrounding immediate consequences.

The rejection is correct: the definition of infimum gives no existence theorem, so the approximation number was not yet defined.  I added the real infimum-property theorem and verified nonemptiness and the lower bound before introducing a_n; I also field-qualified every dimension.

The mathematical characterization was sound after an index shift, but the rejection correctly flags an interface violation: a library sequence starts at zero.  I retained positive-indexed families and explicitly defined their shifted scalar series and the zero-based partial-sum sequence R_0,R_1,... .

The rejection is correct about the notation: this library defines the trace norm only after trace-class membership, so assigning it the extended value infinity is ill-typed.  The divergent harmonic singular-value series alone proves the counterexample and has replaced that assignment.

The rejection is correct against the cited nuclear interface: a coefficient at index zero is absent from its positive-indexed sum, so the displayed representation had every included term equal to zero.  I moved the sole term to index one and verified the resulting zero-based partial sums.

The rejection correctly identifies an unlicensed restatement: the cited Hilbert-Schmidt theorem requires supplied bases.  Those Hilbert-Schmidt assertions are not used anywhere in this trace-class proof, so I removed them and retained only the basis-free adjoint-norm and composition facts actually consumed.

The rejection is correct: a finite- or zero-dimensional reproducing-kernel space cannot have an orthonormal basis indexed by all naturals.  The trace-class argument depended on that family, so I replaced it by an empty, finite, or countable basis and a separate zero-padded positive indexing for the nuclear representation.

The representative chain-rule computation was correct, but the rejection correctly notes that it was called an equality on quotient classes before equivalence and chart independence had been proved.  I reordered the proof so those foundations precede and explicitly license functoriality.

The rejection is correct and affects the theorem, not merely the proof: under the supplied structured-manifold interface, postcomposition need not produce an atlas member, so an arbitrary nonmaximal atlas need not contain any straightening chart.  I added maximality of M's specified atlas and proved compatibility before invoking it.

The rejection is correct: invoking the regular-value theorem only at C^1 regularity cannot establish a smooth submanifold.  I now keep the local representative smooth and apply that theorem with k=infinity; I also propagated its newly explicit maximal-domain-atlas hypothesis.

The rejection is correct under the specified-atlas convention: translating an atlas chart need not yield another member, so the demanded centred charts might not exist.  I now choose arbitrary atlas charts and perform affine translations solely inside the Banach-space representative, without relabelling them as manifold charts.

The rejection is correct: for B:X times Y to Z, the expression B(x,x) has no type unless x belongs to both input spaces.  I restricted the diagonal specialization to X=Y, where x↦(x,x) is a bounded linear map into X times X and the chain rule applies.

The rejection is correct: the closed-subspace completeness theorem cannot be applied until completeness of ell-infinity is supplied.  I proved ell-infinity completeness inline from scalar completeness and Replacement, retained the direct c_0 completeness result, and only then used the closed-subspace theorem.

reviews.reason: The repaired proof now establishes uniqueness for the actual directed net: the union of two finite tail indices lies in both tails, forcing the two proposed limits arbitrarily close.  The inverse definition and all later limit passages are consequently well-defined.

The conclusion now distinguishes a nonempty kernel basis from the injective case.  For every b in B, unit norm gives b nonzero and Tb=0, while B is empty when the kernel is zero; all basis and spanning arguments are otherwise unchanged.

The definition now fixes one field F for H and K and writes dim_F E_lambda(|T|).  Its extra finite-rank and decay claims now cite finite-rank compactness and the nth-term test, so each stated immediate consequence has the premise it needs.

The candidate norm set contains the zero operator and lies in the nonnegative reals, so the cited infimum theorem now supplies existence and the definition supplies the lower-bound comparisons.  The upper and lower approximation inequalities then prove equality without an existence gap.

The carrier now distinguishes positive-integer-indexed families from sequences.  It defines R_0=0 and R_m as the first m terms for m at least one, and interprets every nuclear sum through the zero-based shifted sequence indexed by m in N.

The proof now states that the positive singular values are 1/n and that their harmonic series diverges, directly negating the trace-class finiteness condition.  It explicitly leaves the trace norm undefined, while the square series still proves Hilbert-Schmidt membership.

The repaired representation uses u_1=v/||v|| and v_1=||v||u, with all terms from index two onward zero.  Consequently R_0=0 and every R_m for m at least one equals T, and the licensed trace formula gives exactly the inner product of u and v.

The facts section and dependency list no longer claim unqualified Hilbert-Schmidt estimates.  Step 1.3 needs only existence and norm preservation of B*, plus the operator-norm composition inequality; both are now stated with their exact basis-free suppliers.

Parseval and the Hilbert-Schmidt calculation now use the actual basis indexed by an empty, finite, or countably infinite set I.  A distinct family h_j pads finite bases by zero, giving a valid positive-indexed nuclear representation with the required zero-based partial sums in every dimension.

Reflexivity and symmetry now precede transitivity; only then are the differential and vector operations proved independent of representatives.  The identity and composition formulas occur afterward and explicitly invoke that well-definedness, eliminating the circular quotient-level claim.

The theorem now assumes the specified atlas of M contains every compatible C^k chart.  The proof uses a translated compatible source chart, constructs the graph-straightening chart, checks both transitions with every atlas chart are C^k, and only then uses maximality to obtain the required split chart.

For each trivializing neighbourhood, the proof now checks the vertical-derivative hypothesis at every local zero, not only the initially chosen point, and invokes the regular-value theorem at k=infinity.  Maximality of the inherited open-submanifold atlas is also established before that invocation.

The normal form now starts from arbitrary supplied charts, records their coordinate values a and b, and defines the recentered representative by x↦psi(f(phi^{-1}(a+x)))-b.  The proof also restores the missing domain condition in T_0 and field-qualifies all dimensions.

The general derivative formula remains valid for arbitrary X and Y.  The separate diagonal clause now begins with X=Y, explicitly types d:X→Z and x↦(x,x):X→X×X, and derives the displayed formula from the already proved derivative and the chain rule.

Completeness of ell-infinity is now proved inline from scalar completeness and Replacement, and c_0 completeness is explicitly licensed.  The almost-disjoint-set proof was also checked and clarified: common supports are finite even when their enumeration stages differ, and deleting finite intersections proves the exact quotient-norm formula used in the dual argument.
